A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same SealQA study and complete Appendices A-I. Full-text and rendered-page comparisons establish matching scientific content; v4 changes acknowledgments and repaginates the references.

before.justification: V3 reports original model evaluations on SEAL-0, SEAL-HARD, and LongSeal, plus human performance results in Appendix F, Table 12.

after.justification: V4 retains these original model evaluations, human performance results, and supplementary empirical analyses.

M1.justification: Benchmark construction, document selection, model evaluation, and answer-grading procedures are unchanged. No algorithm or model component is introduced or revised.

E1.justification: Both versions use SEAL-0 with 111 questions, SEAL-HARD with 254 questions, and LongSeal with 254 questions. Domains, question categories, and evaluated search scenarios are unchanged.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged throughout the main text and appendices, including the evaluated model families, FreshPrompt, Self-Ask, built-in search, and human comparisons.

E3.justification: Section 3.1 retains identical evaluation settings, including LongSeal's 12, 20, and 30 hard negatives and the human study with five researchers answering 50 questions. Additional acknowledgment names do not establish a changed study sample.

E4.justification: The test-time scaling, repeated-sampling, distractor-position, gold-document-only, category breakdown, and qualitative analyses are unchanged, including their appendix evidence.

E5.justification: Repeated-attempt counts and statistical reporting are unchanged, including five samples per model in the repeated-sampling experiment. No seed information, uncertainty estimates, or significance tests are added.

E6.justification: Numerical and qualitative results match throughout. For example, Table 1 retains GPT-5-HIGH's 43.2% SEAL-0 accuracy with search, and Table 12 retains human averages of 38.8% with open search and 50.4% with oracle URLs. Appendix figures and result tables are unchanged.

T1.justification: Task definitions and mathematical statements are unchanged. Neither version introduces original theoretical results or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain identical contributions and claims about benchmark difficulty, vulnerability to noisy retrieval, unreliable test-time scaling gains, and LongSeal relevance-selection failures.

C2.justification: Interpretations of retrieval noise, reasoning failures, and positional effects remain unchanged. Qualifications about benchmark size, possible contamination, and agentic access to released data are also retained.

D1.justification: V4 newly identifies Virginia Tech's Advanced Research Computing as providing computational resources and support, with a footnote link. This is limited disclosure of computing support; hardware specifications, implementation settings, and dataset access information remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 4, research positioning, and the bibliography contain the same works and arguments. The added computing-support link and funding acknowledgment do not introduce related research.

P1.justification: V4 expands the acknowledgments with computing support, Google DeepMind and Google Research funding, and three additional people involved in human evaluation. It also makes small wording corrections and updates the arXiv stamp; scientific prose and section organization remain unchanged.

P2.justification: References move from page 11 to a separate page 12 and reflow, shifting the appendices by one page. The expanded acknowledgments add a footnote. Figures, table structures, captions, and scientific page layouts otherwise match.

improvement.justification: V4 improves attribution and disclosure of support, but the main scientific content and Appendices A-I retain identical methods, evidence, claims, and interpretations. These acknowledgment additions and limited layout changes do not meaningfully alter overall paper quality.
